prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Summary of the 2010 manifesto (policies only, with ideological framing removed)

- Defence and security
  - End involvement in Afghanistan; avoid conflict with Iran.
  - Withdraw troops from Germany; renegotiate NATO terms.
  - Increase defence spending by inflation +1% for five years; maintain an independent nuclear deterrent; strengthen the Navy; restore historic regiments.
  - Introduce a compulsory one-year community service scheme for school leavers.

- Immigration, asylum, and borders
  - Halt most new immigration, with limited work and study exceptions.
  - Deport illegal immigrants and foreign nationals convicted of crimes; impose lifetime re‑entry bans for immigration law violations.
  - End asylum claims not made in the first safe country; no amnesties.
  - Incentivise voluntary resettlement; expand border control capacity.
  - Review citizenship grants since 1997.
  - Halt immigration from Muslim‑majority countries; deport radical Islamist preachers and attendees at their sermons.
  - Repeal race/equalities legislation; restrict multilingual official documents to UK indigenous languages.

- European Union and foreign policy
  - Withdraw immediately from the EU; oppose the euro; negotiate independent trade deals; redirect membership costs to domestic needs.
  - Adopt a non‑interventionist foreign policy; end foreign aid and link any assistance to resettlement aims.

- Constitution, law, and civil liberties
  - Create an English parliament; form a pan‑British parliament for shared matters; reform the House of Lords with non‑party experts.
  - Introduce citizens’ initiative referenda; a new Bill of Rights; recall of MPs; updated treason laws.
  - Restrict postal voting; forbid third‑party election interventions.
  - Repeal the Human Rights Act; withdraw from the ECHR; oppose ID cards and surveillance laws.

- Media and democracy
  - Criminal liability for knowingly false reporting; independent complaints body with right of reply and compensation.

- Culture and civil society
  - Emphasise traditional civility in schools and services; expand teaching of national history and culture.
  - Support high streets (levy on large supermarkets) and protect pubs (tax relief, supervised smoking rooms, lower pub alcohol duty); add patron‑saint bank holidays.

- Crime and justice
  - Refocus policing on crime prevention; reduce bureaucracy.
  - Reintroduce corporal punishment and capital punishment for specified offences.
  - Strengthen householders’ self‑defence rights; ensure full sentence service; expand drug rehabilitation.
  - Establish a remote penal facility for repeat violent offenders; require prison work programmes.

- Health
  - Protect a free NHS; clear deficits by reallocating foreign aid; cut bureaucracy; oppose PFI.
  - Curb “health tourism”; prioritise domestic recruitment; restore ward‑based cleaning; keep local hospitals.

- Education
  - Restore traditional curricula, A/O‑levels, streaming, grammar schools, competitive sport.
  - Expand apprenticeships; subsidise STEM; free university for those completing community service; reopen special needs schools; daily assemblies on traditional values.

- Transport
  - Reverse rail privatisation; invest in high‑speed maglev; reopen lines; upgrade waterways.
  - Replace vehicle excise duty with fuel‑based funding; reduce fuel tax burden; raise motorway speed limit to 90 mph; charge foreign trucks.

- Agriculture and fisheries
  - Replace CAP with a UK system; support family farms; ban GM crops; soil renewal; encourage organic methods.
  - Ban non‑stunned ritual slaughter.
  - Restore a 200‑mile exclusive fishing zone; enhance conservation.

- Energy
  - Expand nuclear power under British ownership; modern clean‑coal; oppose wind expansion and carbon‑credit schemes; fund wave/hydrogen research.

- Economy and tax
  - Cut spending on EU costs, foreign aid, climate programmes, overseas wars, immigration/asylum, and quangos; protect frontline services.
  - Raise personal allowance to £12,500; reintroduce a married allowance; lift inheritance tax threshold to £1m; cut council tax via programme reductions.
  - Separate retail and investment banking; strengthen capital rules; curb bonus culture; review PFI; oppose privatising natural monopolies (e.g., post, rail).
  - Vet foreign takeovers for national/public interest; apply selective tariffs tied to labour and environmental standards; ease regulation on SMEs; support co‑ops; consider limited sovereign money issuance.

- Local economies
  - Expand autonomous credit unions; explore voluntary local currencies.

- Pensions and care
  - Raise state pension to £150/week and link to earnings; gradually raise retirement age; tighten eligibility to citizens and full contributors; reduce the annual tax‑relief cap on pension contributions; oppose any EU‑wide pension bailouts; end forced home sales for care.

- IT and digital
  - Invest in technology universities; protect local IT jobs; nationalise telecoms infrastructure to deliver universal 100 Mbps broadband.
  - Guarantee personal data access rights; target uploaders in anti‑piracy enforcement; scrap national ID database.

TEXT_F:
Summary of proposals and commitments

- Economy and public finances: Support the recovery before tightening from 2011–12; more than halve the deficit by 2014 via growth, fairer tax increases (including National Insurance), cuts to lower-priority spend, £15–20bn annual efficiencies, asset sales, a 1% public‑sector pay cap (2011–13), and public‑sector pension reforms. Protect frontline spending on childcare, schools, the NHS and policing.

- Banking and industry: Tougher bank regulation, capital and “living wills,” a global levy, stronger competition, and disposal of state stakes. Create UK Finance for Growth (£4bn) to channel capital to SMEs and high‑tech firms; expand R&D tax credits, capital allowances and a “patent box.” Tighten takeover rules (two‑thirds shareholder support) and promote employee ownership.

- Jobs, welfare and skills: Future Jobs Fund (200,000 jobs); youth job/training guarantee at six months, mandatory by ten; guaranteed work after two years’ unemployment. Minimum wage to rise at least with average earnings; £40/week Better Off in Work guarantee; expand apprenticeships, technician routes and Skills Accounts; reform incapacity benefits with reassessments and more support to work.

- Infrastructure: High Speed Rail from London to Midlands and North with through‑services to Scotland; Crossrail completion; key rail electrification; motorway hard‑shoulder running; no national road pricing; a third runway at Heathrow with conditions. Universal broadband via a modest landline levy; Green Investment Bank; modernised energy grid.

- Housing and consumer finance: Two‑year stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (funded by 5% rate over £1m); more affordable and social homes; council house building enabled; stronger repossession protections; private rented sector standards and a national landlord register. Transform the Post Office into a People’s Bank; universal right to a basic bank account; support for affordable credit and action on high‑cost lending; portable account/ISA numbers.

- Education: Increase frontline funding for Sure Start, childcare, schools and 16–19; expand free nursery places (age two) and 15 hours for ages 3–4. One‑to‑one/small‑group catch‑up; personal tutors in secondary; powers to replace weak school leadership; growth of accredited school groups; fair admissions; pupil premium locally; strengthened SEN support. Participation to 18; major expansion of advanced apprenticeships; HE funding review with widened access.

- Health and care: Protect NHS spending; up to £20bn efficiencies reinvested. Patient guarantees: 18‑week treatment or funded private care; one‑week cancer test results; over‑40s health checks; choice of any qualified provider; more diagnostics; expanded psychological therapies; more care at home; personal care plans and budgets. Create a National Care Service: from 2011 free home care for highest needs; from 2014 cap residential costs after two years; long‑term move to comprehensive, free‑at‑point‑use care for eligible adults.

- Families and older people: A flexible paid “Father’s Month”; a £4/week Toddler Tax Credit; extend flexible working (including older workers); end default retirement at 65; re‑link Basic State Pension to earnings from 2012; expand low‑cost pension saving; NI credits for caregiving grandparents.

- Policing, justice and immigration: Maintain police/PCSO numbers; neighbourhood policing with accountability; performance “report cards” and powers to replace failing leadership. Early intervention for troubled families; faster, stronger action on anti‑social behaviour, including victim injunctions; expand Community Payback. Use of CCTV and DNA with safeguards; voluntary ID scheme; court and legal aid efficiencies; stronger victim support. Control immigration via a points‑based system, tougher English requirements, stronger borders, and focusing access to entitlements on citizens/permanent residents.

- Environment and rural: Aim for ~40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 (renewables, nuclear, CCS); Green Investment Bank; home “pay‑as‑you‑save” upgrades, smart meters; move toward zero waste; expand habitats, protect Green Belt, increase woodland; fairer food chain (supermarkets ombudsman), clearer origin labelling; CAP and fisheries reforms.

- Culture, sport and communities: Deliver 2012 Olympics legacy; expand school/community sport; enable supporter trusts to buy stakes in clubs; maintain free museum entry and arm’s‑length governance; protect post offices and pubs; uphold BBC independence; support film and video games industries.

- Governance, local power and global role: Referenda on Alternative Vote and a reformed, elected second chamber; fixed‑term parliaments; lobbying register and tighter rules on outside jobs; recall for serious misconduct; expand open data. Stronger local government powers and city‑region devolution; urban transport upgrades; keep council tax rises low. Afghanistan strategy focused on training and transition; Strategic Defence Review; maintain nuclear deterrent; improved support for forces and veterans. Active EU engagement; counter‑terrorism and non‑proliferation; commit 0.7% of national income to aid by 2013 in law; focus on health, education, water/sanitation, anti‑corruption; pursue reform of UN, IFIs, G8/G20 and NATO.
